title: Ordinary alteration covering certificates persist under close henselian approximation
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent henselian Noetherian local domain [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\widehat S=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, where $\widehat A$ is the maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Write $\widehat A=\varinjlim_\alpha A_\alpha$ as the directed union of its finite type $A$-subalgebras, with inclusions $s_\alpha:A_\alpha\to\widehat A$. Give a finite ordinary alteration covering $(X_i\to\widehat S)_{i\in I}$ [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology] and any finite type model $(X_{i,\alpha_0}\to\operatorname{Spec}A_{\alpha_0})_i$ with specified base-change isomorphisms to the $X_i$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist $\alpha_1\geq\alpha_0$ and $N_0\geq1$ such that for every $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$, $N\geq N_0$, and $A$-algebra map $u:A_\alpha\to A$ satisfying $\iota(u(b))-s_\alpha(b)\in\mathfrak m^N\widehat A$ for every $b\in A_\alpha$, the schemes $X_{i,u}=X_{i,\alpha_0}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_{\alpha_0}}S$ have finite generic fibres and $(X_{i,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}\to S)_i$ is an ordinary alteration covering. Here $\iota:A\to\widehat A$ is canonical and $X_{i,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}$ is the reduced induced closed subscheme on the union of global irreducible components dominating $S$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-irreducible-components]; empty members may be omitted. No regularity or boundary assumption is imposed on the given family, and no prime or degree restriction is imposed.

source.place: Expose III Proposition 3.1(i),(ii), printed pp.37--38, applied to the disjoint union of a finite family; ordinary-alt alternative, with no invertible prime assumption.

proof.text: By [lem-per-henselian-excellent-completion-domain], $\widehat A$ is a domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] it is Noetherian and complete for $\mathfrak m\widehat A$: $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated and $A/\mathfrak m$ is a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] that ideal is its maximal ideal. Thus [lem-per-complete-local-excellence] makes $\widehat A$ excellent. Apply [lem-per-ordinary-alteration-proper-refinement] to the given family over $\widehat S$. Obtain a nonempty integral $P$, a proper surjection $p:P\to\widehat S$ with finite function-field extension, a finite open cover $P=\bigcup_jV_j$, and maps $h_j:V_j\to X_{i(j)}$ over $\widehat S$.

source.place: III Proposition 3.1, pp.37--38, opening observation and ordinary standard refinement; II Theorem 3.2.1, p.29

proof.text: All schemes of finite type over the Noetherian bases here are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Their structure maps are locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], and quasi-compact by finite type; and quasi-separated as morphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1); hence they are of finite presentation, without any separatedness hypothesis on $X_i$. By [thm-pd-spreading-out], descend the objects $P,V_j$ to a common stage, retaining the prescribed models of $X_i$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-diagram-lift-of-models] to descend $v_j:V_j\to P$, $h_j$, and their equations over the base with these fixed object models. These are finite diagrams of finite-presentation schemes over affine qcqs bases with affine transition maps.

source.place: III section 2, p.36, finite models and morphisms; Stacks Tag 01ZM (limits.tex, lemma-descend-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Increase the stage so $p_\alpha:P_\alpha\to S_\alpha$ is proper, using [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper]. The original open cover is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and completely decomposed: for any $z\in P$, an open containing $z$ gives a lift with identical local ring and residue field. Apply [lem-per-nisnevich-cover-limit-descent] to arrange that $(v_{j,\alpha}:V_{j,\alpha}\to P_\alpha)_j$ is a completely decomposed etale family. All its models are finite type over Noetherian $S_\alpha$, as required there. At any further common stage properness persists by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and the completely decomposed etale assertion persists by the explicit quantifier of the Nisnevich descent node.

source.place: III proof of Proposition 3.1(ii) and Lemma 3.1.1, p.38; Stacks Tag 081F (limits.tex, lemma-eventually-proper)

proof.text: Set $\widehat K=\operatorname{Frac}\widehat A$. By [lem-per-generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion], each $X_i$ has finite generic fibre: the hypotheses on all component generic points are exactly its alteration-object condition. The same applies to $P$: its unique generic point maps to the generic point of $\widehat S$ by surjectivity and continuity, and its function-field extension is finite. For $T=P$ and every $X_i$ let $d_T$ be the dimension of its finite generic-fibre algebra over $\widehat K$. It is finite locally free of degree $d_T$ over this field [def-pc-finite-locally-free]; $d_P>0$ by surjectivity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free] to $T\to\widehat S$ and the system $D(b)$, $0\ne b\in\widehat A$, whose limit is $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat K$. It gives a nonzero $a_T$ on whose principal open $T$ is finite locally free of degree $d_T$.

source.place: III Proposition 3.1(i), pp.37--38, finite free restriction on a nonempty principal open; Stacks Tag 06AC (limits.tex, lemma-descend-finite-locally-free)

proof.text: Enlarge the index to include all the finitely many $a_T$ in $A_\alpha$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free] to the localized model system $(A_\alpha)_{a_T}$, with limit $\widehat A_{a_T}$, to descend each finite locally free restriction and its degree $d_T$. Choose a common stage $\alpha_1\geq\alpha_0$ satisfying these conditions and Step 3. The finite locally free conditions survive increasing the stage: finiteness survives arbitrary base change by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], while on affine charts a local module basis tensors to the same basis and therefore preserves flatness, finite presentation and rank. This last assertion is the direct local-basis verification from [def-pc-finite-locally-free], not an extra approximation claim.

source.place: III Proposition 3.1(i), pp.37--38, descent of finite free restrictions; Stacks Tag 06AC (limits.tex, lemma-descend-finite-locally-free)

proof.text: For every nonzero $a_T\in\widehat A$, choose $N_T\geq1$ whose coordinate in $A/\mathfrak m^{N_T}$ is nonzero. Such a coordinate exists since completion is the ring of compatible sequences [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $N_0=\max_TN_T$. For $N\geq N_0$ and $u$ as in the statement, the values $\iota(u(a_T))$ and $a_T$ have the same $N_T$-coordinate: $\mathfrak m^N\widehat A$ maps to zero in $A/\mathfrak m^{N_T}$. Thus $u(a_T)\ne0$ in $A$. For every $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$ restrict $u$ to $A_{\alpha_1}$; its congruence remains true, and all specialized diagrams are the same by the associativity of the fibre products defining them. Hence it suffices to use the fixed stage $\alpha_1$ in the remaining steps.

source.place: III Proposition 3.1(i), pp.37--38, the nonvanishing congruence bound

proof.text: Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$. Since every $u(a_T)\ne0$, the induced map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S_{\alpha_1}$ factors through every relevant $D(a_T)$. Each $(T_u)_\eta$ is therefore finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], and has coordinate-algebra dimension $d_T$ by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]: first take its fibre at the image point, then extend the residue field to $K$, tensoring a basis. In particular $(P_u)_\eta$ is nonempty since $d_P>0$. The scheme $P_u$ is proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. By [lem-per-finite-generic-dominant-parts], $Q=P_u^{\mathrm{dom}}$ and each $X_{i,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}$ are objects of $\operatorname{alt}/S$. The same node defines $Q$ as a reduced closed subscheme of $P_u$, so $Q\to S$ is proper by closed-immersion properness and composition. By the generic-fibre identification in [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection], $Q_\eta\simeq((P_u)_\eta)_{\mathrm{red}}$, so it is nonempty. Its image contains the generic point and is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence is all of the integral $S$. Thus $Q\to S$ is a singleton ordinary alteration covering [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology].

source.place: III proof of Proposition 3.1(ii), p.38, specialized proper covering certificate, with no degree restriction

proof.text: Base-changing the etale covering family of Step 3 along $u$ gives a jointly surjective etale family $(V_{j,u}\to P_u)_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. Since $P_u$ has finite generic fibre, [lem-per-finite-generic-dominant-parts] gives finite generic fibres for every $V_{j,u}$ and makes each $V_{j,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}$ an alteration object. By [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection], its etale comparison identifies $V_{j,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}$ with $V_{j,u}\times_{P_u}Q$. Another application of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] now makes $(V_{j,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}\to Q)_j$ jointly surjective etale. This is an ordinary covering by its defining generators [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology].

source.place: III proof of Proposition 3.1(ii), p.38, the covering leg after dominant reduction; II 1.2.5--1.2.8

proof.text: Functoriality in [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection] restricts each $h_{j,u}$ to $V_{j,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}\to X_{i(j),u}^{\mathrm{dom}}$. Let $R$ be the sieve generated by the latter family. Its pullback along $Q\to S$ contains the covering family of Step 8. For every arrow in the sieve generated by $Q\to S$, write that arrow as $Q\to S$ composed with an arrow into $Q$; its pullback of $R$ is covering by stability under pullback. Transitivity in [def-weil-pbc-topos] therefore says $R$ is covering, since $Q\to S$ covers by Step 7. Here upward closure follows directly from those axioms: a sieve containing a covering sieve pulls back to the maximal sieve along every arrow of the smaller sieve, so transitivity applies. This proves the desired family covers, with all its members already alteration objects by Step 7. Empty members may be omitted: their identity is covered by the empty etale family, and transitivity removes these arrows. No prime or degree condition was used.
